Select the Optimal Biological Dose of BOIN12 Trials

Source: R/boin12_select_obd.R
boin12_select_obd.Rd

Select the optimal biological dose (OBD) from the final data of one or more trials of the BOIN12 design with the two-step procedure of Lin et al. (2020): the MTD from the isotonic DLT rates, then the admissible dose up to the MTD with the highest estimated utility.

Usage

boin12_select_obd(
  n_pts,
  n_tox,
  n_resp,
  n_tox_resp = NULL,
  target,
  target_resp,
  cutoff_eli = 0.95,
  cutoff_eli_resp = 0.9,
  psi00 = 40,
  psi11 = 60,
  benchmark_weight = 0.5,
  utility_prior = c(1, 1),
  est_method = c("posterior_mean", "observed", "tail_probability"),
  early_stop = NULL
)

Arguments

n_pts

Integer vector of patients treated at each dose, or a matrix with one row per trial.

n_tox, n_resp

DLT and response counts of the same shape as n_pts.

n_tox_resp

Counts of the patients with both a DLT and a response, of the same shape as n_pts, or NULL. Needed unless psi00 + psi11 is 100, in which case the utility depends on the margins alone. Defaults to NULL.

target

Numeric scalar. Highest acceptable DLT probability, called phi_T by Lin et al. (2020). It is the target of the BOIN boundaries lambda_e and lambda_d, of the admissibility of a dose and of the MTD that bounds the OBD. Lin et al. recommend a value slightly above the target of a design that only considers toxicity, for example 0.35 instead of 0.30.

target_resp

Numeric scalar. Lowest acceptable response probability, phi_E. Note that this is a lower limit, as in sim_bf_boin_et, whereas the target_resp of sim_boin_et is a target.

cutoff_eli

Numeric scalar. A dose is inadmissible, together with every higher dose, when the posterior probability that its DLT rate exceeds target is at least this cutoff. Defaults to 0.95.

cutoff_eli_resp

Numeric scalar. A dose is inadmissible when the posterior probability that its response rate is below target_resp is at least this cutoff. Defaults to 0.90.

psi00, psi11

Numeric scalars from 0 to 100. Utility of a patient without DLT and without response, and with both. The utility of a response without DLT is 100 and that of a DLT without response is 0. Default to 40 and 60, the example of Lin et al. (2020).

benchmark_weight

Numeric scalar above 0 and at most 1. The utility benchmark is benchmark_weight * u_low + (1 - benchmark_weight) * 100, where u_low is the expected utility of a dose whose DLT and response probabilities are target and target_resp, the two outcomes being independent. Defaults to 0.5, the benchmark of Lin et al. (2020); Lu et al. (2025) use 0.6.

utility_prior

Numeric vector of two positive numbers. Beta prior of the utility of a dose divided by 100. Defaults to c(1, 1).

est_method

Character scalar. Estimate of the utility of a dose: "posterior_mean" (the default), the posterior mean of the quasi-binomial model given in Section 4 of the Supplement of Lin et al. (2020); "observed", the observed mean utility, which the example of Section 6 of that Supplement reports; or "tail_probability", the desirability used during the trial, which the 'escalation' package uses.

early_stop

Logical vector or NULL. TRUE for the trials stopped early, which select no OBD. Defaults to NULL, no early stop.

Value

A list with components

obd

Integer vector of the selected dose levels, NA when no dose is selected.

reason

Character vector: "selected", "early_stop" or "no_admissible_dose".

utility

Numeric matrix of the utility estimates (on the scale 0 to 100; for "tail_probability", 100 times the probability), NA for the doses not tried.

Details

Only the doses with at least one patient are considered. The DLT rates are made monotone by isotonic regression with equal weights, and the MTD is the dose whose estimate is closest to target, ties to the higher dose as in the 'escalation' package. The OBD is the admissible dose, in the sense of boin12_simulate, at or below the MTD with the highest estimate, ties to the lower dose. When no dose up to the MTD is admissible, no OBD is selected.

References

Lin, R., Zhou, Y., Yan, F., Li, D. and Yuan, Y. (2020). BOIN12: Bayesian optimal interval phase I/II trial design for utility-based dose finding in immunotherapy and targeted therapies. JCO Precision Oncology, 4, 1393-1402. doi:10.1200/PO.20.00257

See also

sim_boin12, boin12_simulate

Examples

# The example of Section 6 of the Supplement of Lin et al. (2020)
boin12_select_obd(
  n_pts = c(3, 3, 6, 12, 6), n_tox = c(0, 1, 1, 3, 3),
  n_resp = c(0, 1, 2, 6, 3), target = 0.35, target_resp = 0.25,
  est_method = "observed"
)
#> $obd
#> [1] 4
#> 
#> $reason
#> [1] "selected"
#> 
#> $utility
#>      DL1      DL2      DL3 DL4 DL5
#> [1,]  40 46.66667 53.33333  60  50
#>
